tone_statements.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2015. Lalo dialects across time and space: subgrouping, dialectometry, and intelligibility. Asia-Pacific Linguistics A-PL 22. Canberra: ANU. 260 pp. hdl:1885/95391
tone_statements.quote: Harsh phonation is auditorily weaker in C-LB and MD than in CW-QY, but still phonemically contrastive. In Figure 5-5 and Figure 5-6 below, showing C-LB and MD’s tonal systems, Tone *H in both C-LB and MD is slightly higher than *3, but *L and *2 are indistinguishable in pitch height. Both *H and *L are sometimes heard in citation form with a postvocalic glottal stop, a retention from Proto Lalo. In MD, *H is shorter in duration than *3 at a statistically significant level; *L and *2 are not significantly different, even though *L appears longer in Figure 5-6. In C-LB, there is no significant difference in duration between harsh and modal syllables. In utterance medial form, the contrast between harsh and modal is often neutralised in both MD and C-LB.
tone_statements.locator: p. 120, sec. 5.2.1 'Evidence for PLa tone system from Central Lalo and MD'; tone values in Table 5-3 p. 119; inventory sentence sec. 3.3 p. 44

tone_statements.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2010. Lalo regional varieties: phylogeny, dialectometry, and sociolinguistics. PhD thesis, La Trobe University, Bundoora. 447 pp. doi:10.26181/21844209.v1
tone_statements.quote: The syllable template for MD is similar to Central Lalo, (C)VTP, with 28 initials, 8 vowels, 3 pitch height contrasts, and harsh versus modal phonation. Syllable-final nasals are post-lexical, the result of mergers of a syllable with a following syllabic nasal. There is also NT, syllabic nasals, but phonation is not contrastive. MD’s tonal system corresponds to CW-QY’s, distinguishing three levels of pitch height and harsh versus non-harsh phonation. Acoustic analysis is given in Chapter 5.2.1 on tone change.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3.3 'MD', p. 71; the same sentences recur in Yang 2015 A-PL 22 p. 44 with 'in §5.2.1' for 'in Chapter 5.2.1'
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level pitch heights x harsh/modal phonation (5 categories)

sources.note: sec. 3.3 'MD' pp. 71-74 (PDF 96-99) is the first documentation of Mangdi: (C)VTP syllable, 28 initials, 8 vowels, 3 pitch heights x harsh/modal phonation. Nothing on stress or accent anywhere for MD; the word 'stressed' appears once in the whole thesis, in the Central Lalo (CW-QY) sketch ('Following a stressed syllable, the syllabic nasal loses its syllabicity'). p. 3: Ngwi languages incl. Lalo are 'omnisyllabic', almost every syllable carries a lexical tone.
